newsitem.title: GERMANY: Air India ups ex-Germany cargo rates 10pct.
newsitem.headline: Air India ups ex-Germany cargo rates 10pct.

text.p: Air India will increase ex-Germany air cargo rates by 10 percent from June 1, Germany cargo sales manager, Ruediger Brasche, said.
The hike was tied into new combi and freighter services due to be launched in June and July, he told Reuters.

From June 1, Air India will fly Boeing 747-300 Combi flights twice-weekly to Paris and weekly to Amsterdam with Frankfurt stopovers and will start a weekly B747-200 freighter from Paris via Frankfurt to India on July 1.
"We cannot sell the combis at the old rates. The combis are not viable at the old rates," Brasche said.
Air cargo prices would be increased by 10 percent on average but with different rises for different destinations, he added.

Air cargo market rates to India had stabilised at higher levels since a round of high price rises by airlines including Lufthansa Cargo and KLM Royal Dutch Airlines at the start of the year, Brasche noted.
"Now with this higher capacity back in the market we must see how the market reacts. The hour of truth will come in the next few weeks," he said.
